transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO), Carlos (Platform), Sophie (Security), Hannah (PM)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on access handoff, staging environment readiness, and next steps for a shadow benchmark. Covered VPC peering, KMS key access, latency targets, and pricing tradeoffs for hosted vs dedicated pilot capacity.

Topics:
- Access and credentials status
- Network and peering schedule
- Shadow benchmark plan and acceptance criteria
- Security artifacts and KMS integration
- Next steps and owner commitments

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making the time. quick checkin, hope the week treated you ok. we'll go through access, staging readiness, then bench plan. Liam will take the tech bits.
[00:21] Priya: thanks Maya. yes shuffling folks but we have Carlos and Sophie here. big focus this week is making sure we have the env for a realistic run. timeline still end of month ideally.
[00:38] Liam: cool. just to set expectations the shadow run is low risk, we mirror traffic to your staging and measure p50/p95 and cost per token. we need VPC peering or an egress VPN and the KMS test key access.
[00:55] Carlos: about peering, our infra team flagged a potential IP overlap with one of your subnets, we need the CIDR list. also maintenance windows are limited next week.
[01:12] Maya: noted — we'll share our minimal network diagram and suggested CIDRs after this call, I'll put it in the drive link.
[01:28] Hannah: quick question — are there any code changes needed in our side or just routing and creds?
[01:34] Liam: mostly routing and creds; for best results we'll add a small header to traffic so we can isolate shadow traffic. no model changes required. occasional SDK version can matter but we have fallbacks.
[01:50] Sophie: security here — we need assurance on key lifecycle. is Redwood using our KMS or do you hold the keys? what's the encryption model?
[02:02] Liam: good question. we support two patterns: customer-managed keys in your cloud KMS (recommended for pilot) or Redwood-managed keys. for private we can do bring-your-own KMS with HSM-backed policies. we'll send the KMS integration doc.
[02:20] Sophie: please add a sample policy snippet, we need to show it to audits.
[02:25] Maya: will do.
[02:30] Priya: about latency, what latency numbers should we expect when mirroring? our SLO is p95 < 250ms for UI call paths.
[02:41] Liam: depends on routing and model variant. for a quantized medium-size model on dedicated GPUs we see p95 around 120-180ms with continuous batching tuned. hosted fallbacks can be a bit higher. shadow runs will give us the empirical numbers with your payload.
[02:58] Carlos: and cost? team is sensitive — if we go hosted for pilot, what's the delta vs us running on dedicated reserved infra?
[03:08] Maya: I'll send two kpi scenarios — conservative hosted, and dedicated reserved. short answer: hosted is faster to run but higher per-token; dedicated requires commit but cheaper at scale. we'll attach sample math.
[03:22] Hannah: can we use a tiny sample to sanity check before the full 10k QPS mimic?
[03:29] Liam: yes plan is staged — initial micro-shadow with 100 RPS for sanity, then 1k for calibration, then full profile. we expect the first runs to be under an hour each.
[03:45] Priya: ok that helps. on network, Carlos will need the runbook and a proposed peering window.
[03:52] Carlos: also we have a strict egress NAT gateway constraint, may need to open a route table entry.
[03:58] Liam: understood. We'll include NAT considerations.
[04:05] Sophie: about logs and retention — we need to know what traces you keep and for how long, and how PII is redacted.
[04:14] Maya: Redwood keeps operational logs for X days by default but we can extend for enterprise. raw request bodies are not stored unless customer opt-in for evals; we'll send the security doc.
[04:27] Sophie: please highlight the redaction controls.
[04:30] Maya: will do.
[04:33] Hannah: re: stakeholders, Priya wants an exec checkin after the shadow run to review perf and cost.
[04:42] Priya: yes please. 30 minutes top.
[04:45] Maya: noted, we'll schedule the exec touchpoint for the week after the benchmark.
[04:50] Liam: technical note — for accurate caching behavior we need representative session lengths; please share a sample of anonymized payloads and sequence length distribution. 10k samples is fine.
[05:05] Carlos: we can provide that, will scrub PII.
[05:09] Priya: timeline check — if we do small runs this week, full profile next week, can we hit the end-of-month goal?
[05:16] Liam: yes that's feasible if peering is scheduled early next week.
[05:22] Maya: action items then: we send runbook & network diagram, Bluecrest confirms peering window and CIDRs, Redwood runs micro shadow and returns results, Sophie reviews security docs.
[05:35] Sophie: one more item — do you support SAML SSO for the console? we need RBAC mapping.
[05:42] Maya: yes SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC roles are configurable. we'll include the SSO quickstart.
[05:50] Carlos: on the KMS question, we prefer customer-managed keys. what's the typical trouble we see?
[05:56] Liam: common gotcha is IAM binding scope — the inference runtime needs decrypt access only for ephemeral test requests, not key management. we'll provide an example role with least privilege.
[06:10] Priya: ok, that sounds good. any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:15] Liam: none beyond getting the network and sample payloads.
[06:18] Maya: quick note on pricing — for the pilot size you described we have a 90-day reserved pilot option that gives a blended rate; I'll include it in the followup.
[06:29] Hannah: that will help procurement.
[06:32] Priya: procurement will want a simple cost projection.
[06:35] Maya: we'll include a 3-scenario projection: dev (small), pilot (your expected), and steady-state.
[06:44] Carlos: one more infra nit — do you offer routing via private link or only peering?
[06:50] Liam: we support both VPC peering and cloud-provider PrivateLink equivalents; PrivateLink has slightly different latency characteristics. for compliance, PrivateLink is often preferred.
[07:02] Sophie: please call out data residency impacts if we route through hosted regions.
[07:07] Maya: yes we'll document region controls and fallbacks.
[07:12] Priya: ok let's capture owners.
[07:16] Maya: action items repeated in chat; I'll follow up with links. any last questions?
[07:22] Hannah: none here.
[07:25] Priya: good meeting. thanks all.

[Ending minutes - quick recaps and confirmation of dates]
[41:30] Maya: Recap: Runbook + diagram by 7/21, Bluecrest peering window 7/23, micro-shadow starts 7/24, full profile 7/27, exec review 7/29. We'll share links and pricing scenarios today.
[41:50] Priya: great thanks.
[42:00] Meeting ended.
